text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has turned down a request to lift a ban on the use of fireworks at the Tet lunar new year festival.
-- About 6,000 Vietnamese, mostly from Hong Kong, are expected to come back home from refugee camps in Asian countries.
-- The Ministry of Trade has proposed reducing the export tax on processed products but applying higher tax rates on exports of raw materials.
-- Truong Tan Sang, Ho Chi Minh City's Communist Party chief, has asked domestic businesses to earmark part of their capital for research and development.
-- The Standing Committee of the National Assembly has asked the daily Nhan Dan newspaper to increase its coverage of National Assembly activities.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's People's Council says inadequate capital and poor infrastructure slowed the city's economic growth in 1996.
-- Vietnam expects to spend $24 million on its population control plan in 1997.
-- Vietnam has announced the draft of an ordinance on drug control.
-- Vietnam expects to export around 2.5 million tonnes of rice in 1997.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's biggest corruption trial in 22 years begins today. Twenty people have been brought to court, charged with involvement in embezzlement and corruption.
